summary: Promotional credit not applied after org transfer causing unexpected provisional invoice balance
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightBridge AI reports that a promotional credit (promo-2025-Q4-50) that existed on their original org was not applied after they requested an org transfer (parent->child) on 2026-03-10. As a result their provisional invoice generated 2026-03-11 shows a $4,120 balance instead of approximately $520 expected after promo.

Impact:
- Customer received a provisional invoice with unexpectedly high balance; payments are withheld pending clarification.
- Usage is live for a high-throughput dedicated queue; potential revenue/CS impact.

Environment:
- Dedicated account migration, prod - us-east (us-east-1).
- Affected workloads: nightly batch embeddings + interactive chat routes.

Steps to reproduce (customer workflow):
1) Request org transfer from support portal (ParentOrg -> ChildOrg) 2026-03-10 03:14 UTC.
2) Verify promo credit present in parent org billing page prior to transfer.
3) Complete transfer; keys rotated and new billing relationship created 2026-03-10 03:45 UTC.
4) Run normal workload 2026-03-10 -> 2026-03-11. Provisional invoice generated 2026-03-11 00:00 UTC.

Expected behavior:
- Promotional credit should be ported or re-applied to the new org according to transfer policy, reducing provisional invoice to expected net.

Actual behavior:
- Promo credit not visible on child org billing page; provisional invoice shows full usage charge.
- Our metering logs show credits being applied to the original parent org account ID after transfer.

Attachments / logs provided by customer:
- Provisional invoice PDF (prov-2026-03-11-brightbridge.pdf)
- Screenshot of promo on old org before transfer (promo-snap-20260310.png)
- Transfer confirmation email thread.

Notes:
- Customer is on a dedicated plan with reserved capacity; they need quick resolution to avoid billing/payment escalation to finance.
comments: 2026-03-12 - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged receipt of ticket. Asked customer to confirm org IDs and share transfer confirmation. Requested provisional invoice and promo code. SLA flagged P2.
2026-03-12 - BrightBridge Billing Contact (Elena Ruiz): Provided invoice and promo screenshot. Confirms they performed the transfer on 2026-03-10 and that promo was active until 2026-06-30.

2026-03-13 - Liam O'Connor (Billing Engineer): Noted initial hypothesis: promo object was bound to parent org id and transfer process did not rebind cost-credits; asked SRE to check post-transfer billing reconciliation job run on 2026-03-10 04:00 UTC.

2026-03-13 - SRE (Arjun Patel): Checked reconciliation logs. Found that hourly postback aggregator applied an end-of-day credit sweep which executed against parent org id before transfer record propagation completed. Saved logs to /var/logs/billing/recon/2026-03-10 and raised potential race-condition with org-service event propagation.

2026-03-14 - Maya Chen (Support): Informed customer we are investigating a likely race between org transfer and hourly credit sweep; requested temporary hold on invoice collection while we validate fix. Customer agreed and put payment on hold.
2026-03-14 - Liam O'Connor (Billing Engineer): Created hotfix branch to ensure credit migration step runs before credit sweep job; PR opened for review (see related_github_prs).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 - Hypothesis 1: Credit objects are not normalized to canonical customer billing account id during transfer; postback aggregator references stale id. Evidence: credit applied to old_org_1234 in ledger exports. Ledger extract: ledger_2026-03-11 shows credit lines tied to account=old_org_1234.

2026-03-13 - Hypothesis 2: Hourly credit sweep runs at 04:00 UTC daily; transfer events experienced ~45s delay in downstream billing consumer which allowed sweep to process before migration completed. Observed event lag in Kafka topic 'org-events' partition 14 with 00:45s consumer lag around 2026-03-10 03:45 UTC.

2026-03-14 - Runbook check: Org transfer workflow should mark credits with transfer_id and schedule a credit-migrate job. Found missing migrate job entry for transfer_id t-20260310-77. Root cause likely a transient error in org-service webhook retry that returned 504 and did not requeue. Trace id: trace-8f3a2.

2026-03-14 - Metering dashboard: usage lines are correct; no double-counting observed. Problem localized to credit binding and invoice aggregation stage. Relevant dashboards: https://internal.redwood.ai/dashboards/billing-recon?date=2026-03-10

2026-03-14 - Impact assessment: If unresolved, customer will be charged full amount on final invoice; finance escalation likely. Quick mitigation possible by reissuing credit to child org and reconciling provisional invoice before finalization.
resolution:
Workaround applied 2026-03-14: Billing team reissued promo (promo-2025-Q4-50) to child org account id (child_org_9876) and created an offset line on provisional invoice to reflect expected credit (-$3,600). We put final invoice generation on hold for this account and flagged to finance for manual adjustment.

Permanent fix plan:
1) Backport hotfix to ensure credit-migrate job triggers synchronously before hourly credit sweep; PR opened and under review.
2) Add end-to-end integration test for org transfer event ordering and credit rebinding.
3) Add monitoring alert for 'credit-migrate' failures and org-events consumer lag >30s.

Follow-ups:
- Notify customer once final invoice reflects adjustment (expected by 2026-03-16).
- Postmortem to be created linking this ticket and runbook updates.

Ticket status: In Progress (billing workaround applied).
